_comment: Phase 2 - Noble Society. The player is the heir of the ruling house. They recruit villagers as retainers, appoint them to offices, choose what each one trains, pay wages and keep them loyal. All tuning lives here.

house._income: Gold per day from rents and dues before the Steward's bonus.
house._over_cap: Your renown supports a household of retainer_cap_base + renown / renown_per_extra_retainer (+ the charter's places). You may keep more: each retainer beyond that costs over_cap_upkeep gold a day.

player._comment: Who the player is: the ruling family's scion closest to preferred_age; falls back to the lord.

opinion._comment: Opinion of the player (-100..100), rolled once per villager.

recruit._comment: Who can be asked. Whether they say yes is in data/recruitment.json (motives, offers, promises).
recruit._ward: 10-15 year olds join as pages/wards; a parent decides, weighing the family's motives and their own opinion of you.

wages._comment: Gold per day. Kin of the ruling house serve for free.

training._comment: Points per day toward potential: rate * (gap / potential) * learning * age factor * mentor. Current never passes potential.

offices.name: Steward
offices.description: Runs the estate's rents and ledgers. Raises daily income.

offices.name: Marshal
offices.description: Commands the household guard and trains fighters. Mentors Combat and Leadership.

offices.name: Chancellor
offices.description: Speaks for the house. Earns renown each day and makes recruiting easier.

offices.name: Court Scholar
offices.description: Tutors the household. Mentors Intelligence, Politics and Administration.

offices.name: Master of Works
offices.description: Oversees every building site. Construction runs faster with their Administration.
